correctness.rationale: For fixed conductances the tree Lipschitz norm is exactly the maximum arm slope; explicit one-Lipschitz boundary data saturate each row. A change to normalized length-weighted barycentric variables is invertible on the open simplex, and the nonnegative closure is attained by compactness. The minimal arm-gradient excess is reduced to the one-variable feasible parameter z, whose surplus must be allocated to a shortest arm. The denominator is affine on each active-set interval, so its ratio with z has constant derivative sign; the finite breakpoint formula is rigorous. The one-short-arm threshold follows by explicit evaluation of z*= (k-1)/(k+r) and z=1. Independently constructed original-variable exact rational linear programs matched on 42 configurations, with eight equilateral and 35 transition-family additional checks. These finite checks are supplementary and not claimed as general proofs. The nonattainment of positive conductance optima in the short-arm regime is explicitly distinguished from the attained nonnegative closure.

originality.rationale: The exact unequal-arm positive harmonic conductance optimization, finite water-filling formula, and sharp degeneration/attainment threshold were not implied by inspected earlier general extension, finite-graph optimal-extension or published equal-arm star results. The equilateral Banach endpoint factor is known and is not included as an originality claim. General finite optimization methods provide principles, not an identified closed star-family phase diagram. Closest sources and unresolved bibliographic risks are detailed below.
residual_risks: An unindexed publication might explicitly solve the unequal-arm positive harmonic conductor design or derive the same water-filling formula under linear extension/transport terminology.

General finite linear programming algorithms do imply a computable minimization, so mathematical novelty rests on the explicit arbitrary-arm finite closed reduction and exact geometric conductance phase boundary, not on mere computability.

value.rationale: A complete all-dimension, all-positive-arm-length minimax invariant for harmonic Lipschitz extension gives a provably optimal effective-conductance design with a finite analytic water-filling rule, not merely a numerical linear program. The motivated one-short-arm subfamily has a sharp geometry-controlled change from realizable positive design to only degenerate limiting design; this is a structurally relevant stability/conditioning boundary for branching networks. The known equal-arm value is expressly excluded from the originality claim. The theorem distinguishes uniform positive linear harmonic smoothing from data-adaptive Lipschitz extension, which can be norm-preserving. The result neither needs nor asserts an external downstream theorem.
